tasks.title: Lead status history service method gated by canSeeLeadNumber, creating the new lead-status-event.dto.ts
tasks.objective: LeadsService returns the ordered status events of a lead with the actor name, reading them through this.dataSource.getRepository(LeadStatusEvent) with a left join to users on changedById (no new constructor argument and no module change); like getLeadById it loads the lead and checks canSeeLeadNumber(lead.leadNumber) in the service, answering not found for unknown or out-of-scope leads; the task creates the new response DTO file dto/lead-status-event.dto.ts
tasks.estimate_rationale: One service method that reads events through the injected DataSource (precedent: dataSource.getRepository(Company) in deleteLead) so the positional constructor and leads.module.ts stay unchanged, one DTO and cases in the existing spec whose mocked DataSource gains getRepository
acceptance_criteria: An in-scope lead returns its events ordered by changedAt then id with fromStatus, toStatus, changedAt and changedBy
A lead for which canSeeLeadNumber is false or an unknown id raises LeadNotFoundException
A move with no signed-in user returns changedBy null
The new file dto/lead-status-event.dto.ts is created and defines the response item shape
LeadsService constructor and leads.module.ts are unchanged; the spec mock DataSource provides getRepository for LeadStatusEvent

verification.purpose: history ordering, scope and null actor cases

complexity.justification: Must load the lead, apply canSeeLeadNumber in the service like getLeadById, and join users while keeping unattributed events, which needs some design decisions

scope.justification: A single read method, one DTO and test cases; the entity has only a scalar changedById so the user join lives in the query and no module wiring changes

duration.justification: The write half took one commit; reading the same rows with an existing scope helper is a smaller change
evidence: command:grep -rn LeadStatusEvent src db -l -> only the entity, leads.service.ts, the lead mapper comment, the service spec and the SQL file: no controller or read path

risk.justification: A mistake would expose the history of leads that a restricted user may not see, which is a permissions leak

coupling.justification: The controller and the web contract task both depend on this response shape, so the method and its DTO act as a contract

confidence.justification: The scope pattern for reads by id is already in getLeadById and the service spec runs green, so the work is well understood
evidence: command:npx jest src/modules/leads/lead-management/leads.service.spec.ts -> 1 suite and 15 tests passed, including the status event insert cases

tasks.title: GET :leadId/status-history route guarded by leads:read
tasks.objective: The leads controller exposes GET /leads/:leadId/status-history that inherits the leads:read permission and delegates to the service
tasks.estimate_rationale: A thin route plus controller spec cases; the class-level permission already covers it and the spec harness exists
acceptance_criteria: The route answers 200 with the service result and 404 for a missing lead
The route carries no write or delete permission override so the class-level leads:read applies

complexity.justification: Known pattern: one more read route next to getLeadById using the same decorators

scope.justification: One route and its spec cases, nothing else in the controller changes

duration.justification: Comparable to the other read routes already tested with supertest in the same spec file

risk.justification: A missing or wrong permission decorator would let a user without leads:read see audit data

coupling.justification: Defines the HTTP contract the web client consumes in the next milestone

confidence.justification: Controller and spec harness were read and the class-level permission default is explicit in the file

tasks.title: Verify the delete cascade guarantee on lead_status_events: SQL declaration by command, live delete as an optional owner-gated step
tasks.objective: The repository SQL provably declares lead_status_events.lead_id REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so no explicit deletion code is added; an owner-gated live delete in a non-production database is optional and not run by a scheduler
tasks.estimate_rationale: The grep is seconds; the optional live delete needs a non-production database and the owner, so it is outside the unattended estimate
acceptance_criteria: The grep finds the REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE declaration for lead_id
No explicit deletion code is added to deleteLead
Optional owner-gated step: after deleting a throwaway lead in a non-production database its event count is zero

verification.value: grep -n 'REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE' db/add-lead-sales-fields.sql
verification.purpose: the migration declares the cascade on the lead_id foreign key

verification.value: OPTIONAL, owner-gated: in a non-production database delete a throwaway lead and count its lead_status_events rows
verification.purpose: prove the live database, not the SQL file, removes the audit rows
verification.expected: the event count for the deleted lead is 0

complexity.justification: The code already answers the design question with ON DELETE CASCADE, leaving only a mechanical confirmation query

scope.justification: No repository file changes; the output is a recorded check of one table constraint

duration.justification: A single grep on one file; the optional live delete is owner gated and excluded from the estimate
evidence: command:grep -n 'REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE' db/add-lead-sales-fields.sql -> line 69: lead_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

risk.justification: Only a read only grep is required; the optional live delete targets a throwaway row outside production

coupling.justification: Looks at the same table the history method reads, but changes no shared code and needs no ordering

confidence.justification: The cascade declaration was found by grep and read in the SQL file, but whether production applied it is unconfirmed, hence medium
evidence: command:grep -n 'REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE' db/add-lead-sales-fields.sql -> line 69: lead_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
assumption:the migration was applied to production as written

tasks.estimate_rationale: Follows the converted leads precedent: endpoint, port method, HTTP repository method, mapper and one test with a mocked client
acceptance_criteria: getStatusHistory requests /leads/:id/status-history and maps events to domain objects
A null fromStatus and null changedBy are preserved
The new test file LeadHttpRepository.statusHistory.test.ts is created and passes

verification.purpose: repository request and mapping test created by this task

complexity.justification: Mechanical extension of an existing hexagonal repository with the same mapping style

scope.justification: Four small files gain one entry each and one new repository test file is created

duration.justification: The converted leads view added the same kind of repository method and test in one commit

coupling.justification: Consumes the HTTP contract from the API and is consumed by the hook and component that follow

evidence: command:npx vitest run src/features/leads/infra/http/LeadHttpRepository.converted.test.ts -> 1 test passed with a mocked HttpClientLike

An empty list shows an explicit empty message
A failed request shows an error message instead of a blank panel
The new test file LeadStatusHistorySection.test.tsx is created and passes

scope.justification: Three new files, no change to existing components

duration.justification: The lead detail sections added for owner and follow up fields give a size reference of a similar UI change

coupling.justification: Uses the repository method from the previous task and is mounted by the tab task

confidence.justification: Patterns were read but the visual design of the panel is not yet fixed and mocks of the DI context need care
